goal: Let a recruiter and Para AI jointly manage one candidate across every opportunity they're active in, with Para AI organizing context and handling bounded coordination while the recruiter retains control of relationship-sensitive decisions.
user_segments: Para AI (system actor with bounded autonomy)
success_metrics: Less recruiter time spent coordinating one candidate across roles
Fewer opportunities go stale from missed follow-up
Recruiters keep auto-execution on, not off
Recruiters act on Para AI's recommendations more often than not
Zero relationship-sensitive actions sent without recruiter approval
constraints: Recruiter must remain the decision-maker on relationship-sensitive actions
Para AI actions must be traceable to a specific context source
Take-home exercise scope, no existing internal Paraform spec to reconcile against
One shared candidate record (confirmed); coordination is scoped to the roles the recruiter personally submitted the candidate to
Every submission originates from a recruiter's action and consent — Para AI recommends but never auto-submits (confirmed)
assumptions: Resume and LinkedIn data default to Included in matching; notes and call recordings default excluded
Context comes from resume/LinkedIn structured insights, recruiter-added preferences, and transcript insights when calls are recorded (confirmed)
The private / include-in-matching control is a NEW distinction this design proposes, not existing Paraform behavior (confirmed)
Company-to-opportunity mapping is reliable enough to auto-detect same-company double submission
Auto-executed actions are limited to reversible, logistical communications
Para AI recommends matches beyond the recruiter's current submissions; the recruiter's confirmation is the submission
gaps: No candidate-facing surface defined (assumed subject-only, unconfirmed)
Bulk-approve interaction is underspecified and risks becoming a rubber stamp
"Undo" on auto-executed actions is not literally possible for already-sent communications
Default state of the proposed Include-in-matching toggle (on vs. off) for notes/calls is unresolved
Whether a flat 60-90 day staleness threshold is right for all volatile context or should vary by fact type
How Para AI computes the match score on recommended opportunities (e.g. 8/10) and how to keep it trustworthy rather than a black box
Which state changes trigger a cross-opportunity hold, and how long Para holds a paused action before re-escalating
How the candidate page hands off to Paraform's existing cross-candidate Para review/approve surface
edge_cases: Candidate declines one opportunity while active in others
Source excluded from matching after Para AI already used it in a recommendation
Para AI proposes double submission to the same hiring company
Approval-required action left unactioned past the timeout window
Call recording fails to transcribe or produces low-confidence output
Candidate withdraws from the process entirely
Two recruiters, same candidate, same role — platform-prevented and out of scope (confirmed); one shared candidate record
Para AI recommends a new opportunity match — the recruiter's confirmation is the submission, shown in a distinct Proposed section
Volatile context item ages past staleness threshold — flagged for reconfirmation, matching weight discounted
Durable context item ages — never flagged as stale

critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.question: One shared candidate record or per-recruiter views?
What does 'managing across multiple opportunities' mean?
critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.answer: Coordinating the roles the recruiter personally submitted the candidate to.

critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.question: How are cross-recruiter duplicate submissions / ownership conflicts handled?
critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.answer: Platform-prevented (second recruiter can't submit the same candidate to the same role); out of scope for the take-home.

critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.question: Does Para AI ever initiate a submission on its own?
critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.answer: No — every submission originates from a recruiter's action and consent.

critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.question: Is there a single consistent place to review/approve Para activity?
How much context is structured vs. general logs today?
critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.answer: Structured insights from resume + LinkedIn; preferences added by the recruiter; transcript insights when calls are recorded.

critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.question: Is there a way to mark info private / excluded from Para AI?
critical_questions_answered_by_paraform.answer: That would be a new distinction (this design proposes it).

critical_questions_still_open.question: Should the proposed Include-in-matching toggle default on or off for notes/calls?
Is there any candidate-facing view, or is the candidate strictly the subject?
Is company-to-opportunity mapping reliable enough to hard-block same-company double submission, or a soft warning?

design_risks: Bulk approval without forced per-item review turns the approval gate into a formality
Over-cautious visibility defaults starve Para AI of context and defeat the feature's stated purpose
Labeling a sent-and-undeliverable-to-retract email as 'undo' sets a false expectation and breaks trust when discovered
If the auto-executed vs. approval-required distinction isn't visible everywhere an action appears, recruiters are surprised by actions they didn't know had already gone out
A cross-opportunity hold that pauses too aggressively could feel obstructive — trigger set and hold duration need real-world tuning
A match score shown without a legible 'why' reads as a black box and can erode trust
A staleness indicator not backed by real recency-weighting in the matching logic would mislead recruiters the same way a false 'undo' does
teaching_notes: Confirmed with Paraform: one shared candidate record, coordination scoped to the recruiter's own submissions, Para recommends but never auto-submits, cross-recruiter dedup is platform-handled, a consistent Para review surface exists, and private/exclude-from-Para is a new distinction. An earlier per-recruiter-silo assumption was wrong and was removed throughout. Net-new distinctions (include control, cross-opp hold, match scores, per-call review) are called out as assumptions per the brief's guidance.

The brief's 'Passive Placements' reference implies Para AI already has a submission-recommendation muscle; frame this feature as extending that across concurrent opportunities — Para recommends, the recruiter's action originates every submission — not inventing new AI capability
Approval-required items expand inline on their opportunity row (same fast approve/edit/reject interaction as a triage inbox) rather than living behind a separate Action Queue destination
Auto-executed vs. Recruiter-approval-required is the single most important piece of information architecture and must be a persistent, legible signal everywhere an action or its status appears
Opportunities is the default landing view (task-oriented); Activity and Profile are secondary, on-demand tabs — default design decisions toward keeping recruiters on Opportunities
The whole feature is the candidate page; broader recruiter dashboards are the product around it and out of scope for this take-home

The sharpest expression of 'where Para waits' is the cross-opportunity hold (Para pauses its own actions when an offer lands elsewhere) and the per-call review toggle — dramatize the act-vs-wait boundary, don't just assert it
Para AI has no dedicated page — its presence is signaled inline (persistent indicator + attribution tags) and it can take actions from the Ask Para chat behind the standard approval gate
